result:
I fixed the 11 rules whose behaviour didn't match their docstrings. To check, I wrote a reference version straight from the docstrings (including the module-level rules) and compared all 150 rules against it, from 0 to 399 units plus a few very large amounts, at 13 unit prices. Before the fix, those 11 rules gave different results. After the fix, all 150 match.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | `qty > 12`, so exactly 12 units got no discount | `qty >= 12` |
| 18 | Cap only applied when `disc > 200000`, so discounts from 100,000 to 200,000 won weren't capped | Always `min(disc, 100000)` |
| 28 | Whole rule, but used the marginal formula `(qty - 50) * unit` | `base * 5 // 100` |
| 44 | Used `round()`, which can round up | `base * 10 // 100` |
| 65 | Applied the 30,000 cap to the amount before the discount, not to the discount | Work out the discount first, then `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 79 | Used `round()` | `base * 12 // 100` |
| 91 | `qty >= 13`, so the threshold was one unit too high | `qty >= 12` |
| 105 | Discount rate was 9% instead of 8% | 8% |
| 119 | `qty >= 31` | `qty >= 30` |
| 127 | `qty > 30` | `qty >= 30` |
| 139 | Used `round()` | `base * 15 // 100` |

I also changed rule 15 from `qty > 100` to `qty >= 100` to match its docstring. It's a marginal rule, so the discount at exactly 100 units is 0 either way and its results don't change.

STATUS: DONE
